title: Gebru: technically fair, socially unjust
summary: Gebru's justice problem: a technically fair model (the accuracy gap closed) coordinates with biased deployment in over-policed communities, so the improvement makes surveillance more efficient and wrongful arrests more likely. The missing third body is coordination of technical development with social justice and lived experience.
source: Ch06 — 'How does this AI coordinate with existing power structures, and what does that coordination create for the people it affects?'

nodes.label: Technical Accuracy
nodes.description: Accuracy gap closed: 65% to 95% on Black faces

nodes.label: Disparate Harm
nodes.description: Wrongful arrests (Williams, Parks) in over-surveilled communities

nodes.label: Biased Deployment
nodes.description: Used by police and governments, concentrated in black and brown neighbourhoods

nodes.label: Surveillance Efficiency
nodes.description: More accurate identification of more people

nodes.label: Justice Coordination
nodes.description: Technical development coordinated with social context and lived experience

edges.description: A more accurate system identifies more people more efficiently
Deployment concentrates the capability on already over-policed communities
Efficient surveillance converts into arrests and wrongful arrests
Coordination with social context would redirect or block deployment
Coordination with lived experience would reduce harm

identifiability_note: The absent justice coordination (n5) is a common cause of deployment choices and harm; sometimes the coordination analysis concludes that the technology cannot be made just and should not be built.
